source_columns: BB084, FY105M, FY105Y, FD86M, FD86Y, FD35M, FE86M, FE86Y, FE24MN, SY2M, SY2Y, SY1M, SE2M, SE2Y, SE1M, FUSTTYPE, cohort, wave
expression:
local({
  fy <- if_else(
    as.numeric(FY105M) %in% 1:12 & as.numeric(FY105Y) %in% 50:70,
    1900 + as.numeric(FY105Y) + (as.numeric(FY105M) - 0.5) / 12,
    NA_real_
  )
  fd <- if_else(
    as.numeric(FD86M) %in% 1:12 & as.numeric(FD86Y) %in% 50:70,
    1900 + as.numeric(FD86Y) + (as.numeric(FD86M) - 0.5) / 12,
    NA_real_
  )
  fe <- if_else(
    as.numeric(FE86M) %in% 1:12 & as.numeric(FE86Y) %in% 50:70,
    1900 + as.numeric(FE86Y) + (as.numeric(FE86M) - 0.5) / 12,
    NA_real_
  )
  sy <- if_else(
    as.numeric(SY2M) %in% 1:12 & as.numeric(SY2Y) %in% 50:70,
    1900 + as.numeric(SY2Y) + (as.numeric(SY2M) - 0.5) / 12,
    NA_real_
  )
  se <- if_else(
    as.numeric(SE2M) %in% 1:12 & as.numeric(SE2Y) %in% 50:70,
    1900 + as.numeric(SE2Y) + (as.numeric(SE2M) - 0.5) / 12,
    NA_real_
  )
  fd_date <- if_else(as.numeric(FD35M) %in% 2:6, 1982 + (as.numeric(FD35M) - 0.5) / 12, 1982 + 3.5 / 12)
  fe_date <- if_else(as.numeric(FE24MN) %in% 2:6, 1982 + (as.numeric(FE24MN) - 0.5) / 12, 1982 + 3.5 / 12)
  sy_date <- if_else(as.numeric(SY1M) %in% 2:7, 1984 + (as.numeric(SY1M) - 0.5) / 12, 1984 + 4 / 12)
  se_date <- if_else(as.numeric(SE1M) %in% 2:7, 1984 + (as.numeric(SE1M) - 0.5) / 12, 1984 + 4 / 12)
  case_when(
    wave == "Base year 1980" ~ if_else(as.numeric(BB084) %in% 13:21, as.numeric(BB084) + 0.5, NA_real_),
    wave == "First follow-up 1982" & as.numeric(cohort) == 1 & as.numeric(FUSTTYPE) %in% 2 ~ fd_date - coalesce(fd, fy),
    wave == "First follow-up 1982" & as.numeric(cohort) == 1 ~ 1982 + 3.5 / 12 - fy,
    wave == "First follow-up 1982" ~ fe_date - fe,
    .default = coalesce(sy_date - sy, se_date - se)
  )
})
notes: 1980: 'Age' (BB084), completed years + 0.5; the open bands '13 or younger' (sophomore form), '15 or younger' (senior form) and '21 or older' take 13.5, 15.5 and 21.5 (under 0.5% of answers). Follow-ups: decimal age from the student's birth month and year at mid-month against the questionnaire month at mid-month: 1982 dropouts FD86M/FD86Y against 'today's month' FD35M, 1982 seniors FE86M/FE86Y against FE24MN, 1984 SY2M/SY2Y and SE2M/SE2Y against SY1M and SE1M. The 1982 in-school, transfer and early-graduate sophomores have no questionnaire date (FY105M/FY105Y against mid-April 1982, the midpoint of the documented February-June 1982 sessions; 08896-Codebook.pdf), as have follow-up rows with no questionnaire month (fieldwork midpoints mid-April 1982 and the start of May 1984). Partial: those rows use an assumed reference date. Missing and reserved codes are NA; ages above 19 are kept.

1980 student item 'Sex' (BB083) and the study's sex composites (SEX on 1982 rows, SEXCOMP on 1984 rows, which repeats the 1982 composite); male or female only, self-report with study editing. Modal within participant; ties and no value = Unknown.

local({
  division <- recode_values(
    as.numeric(SCHREGN),
    1 ~ "US: New England",
    2 ~ "US: Middle Atlantic",
    3 ~ "US: South Atlantic",
    4 ~ "US: East South Central",
    5 ~ "US: West South Central",
    6 ~ "US: East North Central",
    7 ~ "US: West North Central",
    8 ~ "US: Mountain",
    9 ~ "US: Pacific",
    default = NA_character_
  )
  region84 <- recode_values(
    as.numeric(HSREG),
    1 ~ "US: Northeast",
    2 ~ "US: North Central",
    3 ~ "US: South",
    4 ~ "US: West",
    default = NA_character_
  )
  value <- case_when(
    wave == "Base year 1980" ~ division,
    wave == "First follow-up 1982" & as.numeric(cohort) == 1 & as.numeric(FUSTTYPE) == 1 ~ division,
    wave == "First follow-up 1982" & as.numeric(cohort) == 2 & as.numeric(FE5) %in% 1:2 ~ division,
    wave == "Second follow-up 1984" & (as.numeric(SY7) %in% 1:2 | as.numeric(SE7) %in% 1:2) ~ region84,
    .default = NA_character_
  )
  coalesce(value, "Unknown")
})
notes: School location standing in for residence, only where the student is still at the high school or lives in the same place or less than 50 miles from it: the base-year school's census division (SCHREGN, nine divisions, 'US: <division>') on 1980 rows, on 1982 rows of sophomores still in their base-year school (FUSTTYPE 1) and of seniors living in the same place as when they were seniors or less than 50 miles from it (FE5 = 1 or 2); the senior high school's census region (HSREG, four regions, 'US: <region>') on 1984 rows living in the same place as that school or less than 50 miles from it (SY7, SE7 = 1 or 2). Unknown elsewhere. Proximate: census groupings of states, and school location. HSDIV (1984) codes only three divisions and is not used; CENRGN repeats SCHREGN.

  "Unknown"
)
notes: 1980 student: 'Were you born in the United States?' (BB044; 1 yes, 2 no per 07896-0002-Codebook.txt student item 214, the table holding no value labels because the sophomore .sav reverses them); multiple punch and missing = Unknown. Carried within participant to 1982 and 1984; base-year non-participants are Unknown.

expression:
local({
  usual <- as.numeric(LB14)
  other <- as.numeric(LB15)
  english <- usual %in% c(1, 12:22) | other %in% c(2, 20:29)
  another <- usual %in% c(2:22, 33) | other %in% c(3:12, 20:72)
  value <- case_when(
    wave != "Base year 1980" ~ NA_character_,
    as.numeric(LANGDATA) == 0 ~ "Country language only",
    !(usual %in% c(1:22, 33)) | !(other %in% 1:72) ~ NA_character_,
    english & another ~ "Country language and another",
    english ~ "Country language only",
    another ~ "Another language only",
    .default = NA_character_
  )
  coalesce(carry_within(value, ID, order = wave), "Unknown")
})
notes: 1980 student items 'What language do the people in your home usually speak?' (LB14) and 'What other language is spoken in your home?' (LB15), country language English. Every student answered the five language questions; only those who gave a non-English answer to any of them have language-file data (LANGDATA 1), so LANGDATA 0 = Country language only (it also holds the few who left all five blank). English usual with no other language = Country language only; English with another language, in either item or a combined code, = Country language and another (LB15 codes 20-29 combine English with another language, 31-72 two other languages); non-English usual language with no English in either item = Another language only; multiple punch and missing = Unknown. Carried within participant to 1982 and 1984 (base-year non-participants Unknown). HOMELANG (1984 rows) is the study's composite of the same 1980 items and is not used.
Only county and state labour-market indicators of the base-year school (unemployment rates, employment growth, per-capita income and wages), not an area SES index on national quintiles.

1980: the study's SES composite (BBSESRAW: father's occupation, father's and mother's education, family income and an additive scale of eight household possessions, each standardised within grade and summed; student report). 1982 sophomores: the first follow-up SES composite built the same way from 1982 data (FUSES; not built for dropouts). Cut 40/20/40 on the unweighted rows within wave (at or below the 40th percentile Low, above the 60th High). 1982 seniors (no composite: too few components were asked) and 1984 rows (young adults, own and spouse's income only, not the family's) are Unknown; household SES is never carried over the 24 months between waves.

(FY100 1982 sophomores, FD4 dropouts, FE4 seniors, SY6 and SE6 1984): rural or farming community = Rural; small city or town (under 50,000), medium-sized city (50,000-100,000) and suburbs of medium, large and very large cities = Suburban; large city (100,000-500,000) and very large city = Urban; military base and missing = Unknown. local({
  father <- coalesce(as.numeric(BB036B), as.numeric(FY52B), as.numeric(FE3B), as.numeric(SY4B), as.numeric(SE4B))
  male <- coalesce(as.numeric(BB036C), as.numeric(FY52C), as.numeric(FE3C), as.numeric(SY4C), as.numeric(SE4C))
  mother <- coalesce(as.numeric(BB036D), as.numeric(FY52D), as.numeric(FE3D), as.numeric(SY4D), as.numeric(SE4D))
  female <- coalesce(as.numeric(BB036E), as.numeric(FY52E), as.numeric(FE3E), as.numeric(SY4E), as.numeric(SE4E))
  structure <- case_when(
    !(father %in% 0:2 & mother %in% 0:2) ~ "Unknown",
    father %in% 1 & mother %in% 1 ~ "Two biological/adoptive parents",
    (mother %in% 1 & male %in% 1) | (father %in% 1 & female %in% 1) ~ "Step family",
    mother %in% 1 | father %in% 1 ~ "Single parent",
    .default = "Other"
  )
  adult <- wave == "Second follow-up 1984" | (wave == "First follow-up 1982" & as.numeric(cohort) == 2)
  if_else(adult & structure == "Other", "Unknown", structure)
})
notes: 'Which of the following people live in the same household with you?' (BB036 1980) or lived with you in the first week of February (FY52 1982 sophomores, not dropouts; FE3 1982 seniors; SY4 and SE4 1984): father and mother = Two biological/adoptive parents; one parent with an other guardian of the other sex (stepfather or foster father; stepmother or female guardian) = Step family; one parent only = Single parent; neither parent = Other; unanswered = Unknown. Proximate: a foster parent beside a parent is coded Step family, the category the structure forces. Not carried. 1982 senior and 1984 young adults living with a parent are coded the same way; those living with neither parent (alone, with a spouse, in a dormitory or barracks, or with others) are Unknown, because their main home cannot be identified.

notes: The study's locus of control composite (BBLOCUS 1980; FYLOCUS 1982 sophomores, FELOCUS 1982 seniors): four agree-disagree items 'Good luck is more important than hard work for success', 'Every time I try to get ahead, something or somebody stops me', 'Planning only makes a person unhappy since plans hardly ever work out anyway' and 'People who accept their condition in life are happier than those who try to change things' (BB058B, E, F, G and their 1982 copies), each standardised within grade and combined (07896-0002-Codebook.txt student item 514).
